BiblicalUsage: In Daniel's Aramaic this is the word for going in, and Daniel does it twice in ways that matter: he goes in to the king to ask for time before the dream is interpreted, and the magicians come in before Nebuchadnezzar and fail where Daniel will succeed. Entering the king's presence is the doorway of the whole book.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for walking through a door carries no deep theology; what it shows is Daniel's nerve, that he went in and asked while the wise men of Babylon could only come in and confess they could not.
RelatedEvents: Daniel's Resolve in Babylon; Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Image
